name: Mohammed V Mausoleum
hero_subtitle: White marble, royal guards and a quiet hall beside Hassan Tower.

overview.title: Modern memory next to medieval ambition
overview.p1: The Mausoleum of Mohammed V holds the tombs of Mohammed V and Hassan II in a white marble pavilion that contrasts with the ruined columns of Hassan Tower outside. It is formal, ceremonial and one of the capital’s most visited interiors.
overview.p2: Inside, zellij, carved plaster and the guarded silence set a different tone from the open esplanade. Photography rules and dress expectations are stricter than at many outdoor sites.
overview.p3: Plan it as a short, focused visit after or before the tower. The combination is the classic Rabat “power and memory” stop on the Bouregreg side of the city.

q1.question: Is entry free?
q1.answer: Access is generally free; follow current rules at the entrance for bags and dress.

q2.question: What should I wear?
q2.answer: Modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is expected. Remove hats inside if asked.

q3.question: Can I take photos?
q3.answer: Rules can restrict photography inside — follow signs and staff instructions.

q4.question: How long is the visit?
q4.answer: Twenty to forty minutes for most visitors.

q5.question: Is it open during prayer times?
q5.answer: Hours can vary on religious days; check locally if your visit falls on a holiday.

food.title: No food inside — plan around the visit
food.p1: Nothing is sold inside the mausoleum. Eat and drink on the avenues before or after, combined with your Hassan Tower stop.
food.p2: Keep bottles out of the formal hall.
food.li1: Coffee before you enter the complex
food.li2: Lunch after both tower and mausoleum
food.li5: Same block as Hassan Tower — one taxi drop-off

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting the Mohammed V Mausoleum

1.title: Dress and bags before you reach the door
1.desc: Cover shoulders and knees; carry a light scarf if needed. Large bags may be checked or restricted. Sorting this at the hotel saves awkward moments at the entrance.

2.title: Quiet is part of the architecture
2.desc: Keep voices low, phones silent, and move with the flow of visitors. The hall is designed for formal respect — treat it closer to a ceremonial space than a museum gallery.

3.title: Do tower and mausoleum as one block
3.desc: Arrive once, see both, then leave for food or the next neighbourhood. Splitting them with a long lunch in between means a second security and heat cycle on the open esplanade.
